label: Copy-phase steps of short (L<=4) sequences
explanation: Update gate z36 is active only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires during the original phase or at the <DEL> step. It fires most reliably on short sequences: about 33% of copy steps when L=3 and 21% when L=4, compared with 2-6% when L>=5. L=3/4 sequences hold about 73% of activation mass. Magnitude is largest at the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1), which holds about 51% of mass; the top examples are all L=3 sequences at that step, and activation falls off over the later recall indices. Within short sequences it is usually weak or off on the final output step. In longer sequences it fires sparsely and weakly on early-to-middle copy steps (recall_idx 1-5), with a mild preference for some input tokens (n, j, c, e); a predicate did not capture this tail. It does not fire on recall_idx 0 or on recall_idx >= 6.
